html:
The Kallawaya are a people of the Andes of Bolivia, in the Bautista Saavedra and Muñecas provinces north of Lake Titicaca. They are famous as travelling healers who walk long distances to treat patients with plants, rituals and amulets.

Their healing knowledge covers hundreds of medicinal plants of the high Andes and the forests below. Healers have travelled widely since at least Inca times, and the tradition is often traced back further, to the era of Tiwanaku. The men speak a secret healers' language, Machaj Juyai, that mixes the grammar of Quechua with words largely from the old Puquina language. In everyday life they speak Quechua, and the region also borders the Aymara.

UNESCO proclaimed the Andean worldview of the Kallawaya a masterpiece of humanity's heritage in 2003.
